xero.why: Core accounting scopes work for any app, but payroll scopes need a payroll-admin user (UK also needs partner access) and some scopes need partner certification or a financial services partnership.

options.quote: Web and PKCE apps – Since March 2026, all new and existing Web and PKCE apps have been assigned granular scopes.
options.note: Granular scope listed with no certification requirement; broad accounting.transactions remains until September 2027.

options.quote: accounting.invoices New View and manage invoices
options.note: Listed among standard organisation scopes.

options.task: Read the profit and loss report
options.quote: accounting.reports.profitandloss.read New View profit and loss
accounting.contacts View and manage your contacts
In addition, only Xero users with payroll administrator access can authorise access to payroll endpoints.
options.note: The NZ payroll overview page was not fetched, so NZ is not confirmed.

options.quote: You'll need partner permissions provided by Xero.
options.note: The UK page also says only payroll administrators can authorise payroll endpoints.

options.quote: To access the Practice Manager API you will need to first register as an app partner and complete a security self-assessment questionnaire.

options.task: Read bank statement and reconciliation data for lending
options.quote: The Finance API is a closed API that is only available to those that have an established (Financial Services) partnership with Xero for lending purposes.
options.note: Bank Feeds (bankfeedsv2) is also limited to financial services partners and approved app partners.

standard.effect: Any Xero app can request it, and a user with the Standard or Adviser role approves it when connecting.
standard.quote: In order to authorise any API connection the Xero user must have the Standard or Adviser role.

payrolladmin.effect: The person who connects the organisation must be a Xero payroll administrator.
payrolladmin.quote: In addition, only Xero users with payroll administrator access can authorise access to payroll endpoints.

partner.effect: You must register as a Xero app partner and get the scope enabled by Xero before you can request it.
partner.quote: The following scopes are only available after additional certification. If you require access to these scopes please let us know once you register to be a partner.

financial.effect: Only a lender or financial institution with a signed financial services partnership with Xero can get this API.
financial.quote: The Bank Feeds API is available to financial institutions with an established financial services partnership with Xero and approved app partners.

dropbox.why: User scopes are approved by each Dropbox user, but team scopes produce a team-linked token that a Dropbox team admin must authorize.

options.quote: Required scope: files.content.read
options.note: User authentication.

options.quote: Required scope: files.content.write
options.note: User authentication.

options.quote: Required scope: files.metadata.read
options.note: User authentication.

options.quote: Required scope: sharing.write
options.note: User authentication.

options.quote: Required scope: members.read
options.note: Endpoint uses Team authentication.

options.quote: Required scope: members.write
options.note: Endpoint uses Team authentication.

options.quote: Required scope: events.read
options.note: Endpoint uses Team authentication.

options.task: Read or write any team member's files
options.quote: Legacy apps must have Team member file access permissions while scoped apps must have the team_data.member scope selected.
options.note: Used with the Dropbox-API-Select-User header on a team token.

user.effect: The signed-in Dropbox user approves the scopes for their own account on the authorization page.
user.quote: This level of access is then communicated to the end user on the Dropbox app authorization page where the user consents to sharing their data.

teamadmin.effect: A Dropbox team administrator must authorize the app, and the token belongs to the whole team.
teamadmin.quote: An app that uses these endpoints will need to be authorized by a team administrator.

github.why: For GitHub Apps, account and repository permissions can be granted by the user or a repo admin, but organization permissions or Repository administration need an organization owner; OAuth app scopes do not change approval.

options.quote: Account permissions allow your app to access resources related to a user if the user has also authorized your app.
options.note: Granted by the user at authorization, not at installation.

options.quote: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} read
options.note: Listed under Repository permissions for Contents; on a personal account the user installs it themselves.

options.quote: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues write
options.note: Listed under Repository permissions for Issues.

options.quote: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls write
options.note: Listed under Repository permissions for Pull requests.

options.quote: If your app only needs "Administration" permission to create repositories, request the "Repository creation" permission instead.
options.note: Administration needs an owner; whether a repo admin can install an app with only Repository creation is not stated.

options.quote: POST /orgs/{org}/invitations write
options.note: Listed under Organization permissions for Members.

options.quote: POST /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/drafts write
options.note: Listed under Organization permissions for Projects.

user.effect: Any user can install the app on their personal account or authorize it to act for them.
user.quote: Anyone can install GitHub Apps on their personal account.

repoadmin.effect: In an organization, a repository admin can install the app on repos they administer, unless the owner has blocked this.
repoadmin.quote: Repository admins can install GitHub Apps in the organization that owns the repository if the app does not request any organization permissions or the "Repository administration" permission.

owner.effect: An organization owner must install the app; other members can only send the owner a request.
owner.quote: Instead of installing the app, GitHub will send a notification to the organization owner to request the organization owner to install the app.

github.notes: OAuth apps are approved per app, not per scope: when OAuth app access restrictions are on, members must request owner approval for any OAuth app.

jira.why: Any user can consent to any scope with no Atlassian review per scope, but admin scopes only work when the consenting user is a project admin or Jira admin.

options.quote: Issues are included in the response where the user has: Browse projects project permission for the project containing the issue.
Permissions required: Browse projects and Create issues project permissions for the project in which the issue or subtask is created.
Permissions required: Browse projects and Add comments project permission for the project that the issue containing the comment is in.

options.task: Register a webhook for issue changes
options.quote: Permissions required: Only Connect and OAuth 2.0 apps can use this operation.
options.note: No admin permission is listed for this operation.

options.quote: Permissions required: Administer Jira global permission or Administer Projects project permission for the project the version is added to.
Permissions required: Administer Jira global permission.
Permissions required: Administer Jira global permission.

user.effect: Any user can consent, and the app can only do what that user's project permissions allow.
user.quote: Note, the permissions held by the user an app is acting for always constrain the app, regardless of the app's scopes.

projectadmin.effect: The person who connects must be an admin of that project (or a Jira admin), or the calls fail.
projectadmin.quote: Permissions required: Administer Jira global permission or Administer Projects project permission for the project the version is added to.

jiraadmin.effect: The person who connects must hold the Administer Jira global permission, or the calls fail.
jiraadmin.quote: For example, if a Jira app has the manage:jira-project scope but the user does not have the Administer Jira permission, the app can not create projects.

salesforce.why: Admin pre-authorization is a per-app Permitted Users policy that each org admin sets, and the OAuth scopes page lists no scope that triggers extra approval.
salesforce.quote: Admin approved users are pre-authorized—Allows only users with the associated profile or permission set to access the app without first authorizing it.

reddit.why: Reddit requires approval for all Data API access, plus separate written approval for commercial use; this depends on purpose, not on the OAuth scopes requested.
reddit.quote: Approval is required: You must request access and get explicit approval before accessing any Reddit data through our API

twitter.why: OAuth scopes need only user consent, but some endpoints are limited to the Enterprise plan whatever the scopes.

options.quote: tweet.write Tweet and Retweet for you.
options.note: Priced per request under pay-per-use (Post: Create).

options.quote: dm.write Send and manage Direct Messages for you.
options.note: Priced per request under pay-per-use (DM Interaction: Create).

options.task: Search posts from the last 7 days
options.quote: Search Posts from the last 7 days. Available to all developers.
options.note: The page lists keys and tokens as a prerequisite but names no specific scope.

options.quote: Full-archive search is available to pay-per-use and Enterprise customers.
options.note: Enterprise gets longer queries (4,096 characters).

options.task: Stream posts matched by meaning (embedding operator)
options.quote: The embedding: semantic operator is available only for Filtered Stream on Enterprise plans with Embedding tier access.
options.note: Basic filtered stream with core operators is available on pay-per-use.

options.task: Stream the full firehose or sampled volume streams
options.quote: To use these APIs, you must first set up an account with our enterprise sales team.

options.task: Listen for post and user compliance events
options.quote: These streams are available with Enterprise access and are designed to help partners that ingest high volumes of data 'listen' for compliance events such as Post edit events.
options.note: Auth type for these streams was not confirmed.

payperuse.effect: Any approved developer account can call it after buying credits, and the user consents to the OAuth scopes.
payperuse.quote: The X API uses pay-per-usage pricing. No subscriptions—pay only for what you use.

enterprise.effect: You must apply to X for an Enterprise plan; no OAuth scope unlocks these endpoints.
enterprise.quote: These endpoints are only available on Enterprise plans:

twitter.notes: Account Activity is listed as Enterprise-exclusive on the Enterprise intro page, but its own page says Enterprise or Pay Per Use access, so it is left out. Pay-per-use is capped at 3 million post reads per month.

figma.why: Most scopes work in any OAuth app (public apps get one Figma review), but some need an Enterprise plan, org:* scopes need an organization admin, and some only work in private apps.

options.task: Read the contents of a file
options.quote: file_content:read Read the contents of files, such as nodes and the editor type.
file_comments:write Post and delete comments and comment reactions in files.
webhooks:write Create and manage webhooks.
file_variables:read Read variables in files. Note: Enterprise plan only.
library_analytics:read Read your design system analytics. Note: Enterprise plan only.
org:activity_log_read Read organization activity logs. Note: Enterprise plan only. Must be an organization admin.
folders:write Create folders. Available only to private OAuth apps in an Enterprise plan.
team_members:write Invite members to teams. Available only to private OAuth apps in an Enterprise plan.

standard.effect: Any OAuth app can request it; a public app needs Figma's one-time review, then each user consents.
standard.quote: When you publish a public OAuth app, Figma reviews it.

enterpriseplan.effect: The scope only works for users on a Figma Enterprise plan.
enterpriseplan.quote: file_variables:read Read variables in files. Note: Enterprise plan only.

orgadmin.effect: The person who connects must be an admin of an Enterprise organization.
orgadmin.quote: org:activity_log_read Read organization activity logs. Note: Enterprise plan only. Must be an organization admin.

privateonly.effect: Only a private app for your own Enterprise team or org can use it, so customers can't connect with it.
privateonly.quote: Private OAuth apps can be used to make requests on behalf of users in team or organization you associated your app with when you created it.
